CUEC: Customers are responsible for reviewing the information security policies and the security capabilities in the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System to determine their applicability and modify their internal controls as appropriate.
Notes: Annual vendor review covers this.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for defining and maintaining policies and procedures governing the customer's administration of access to the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System.
Notes: Access Control Policy covers Workspace admin access.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for establishing documented policies and procedures for the transfer and sharing of information within their organization and with third-party entities.
Notes: Covered by Information Classification Policy; configure domain-level Drive sharing restrictions in Admin Console.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for provisioning maintaining monitoring and disabling end users' access in accordance with their internal access management policies.
Notes: Covered by onboarding/offboarding runbooks.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for provisioning service availability user roles and sharing permissions within the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System consistent with customer organizational policies.
Notes: Role assignments documented in Access Control Matrix.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for implementing secure log-on procedures to access the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System consistent with customer access management policies.
Notes: Enforce 2SV with hardware/passkey via Admin Console.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for provisioning maintaining and disabling end users' access in accordance with customer access management policies.
Notes: Duplicate of CC6.1 row above; tracked in onboarding/offboarding runbook.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for reviewing users' access rights periodically consistent with customer organizational policies to mitigate the risk of inappropriate access.
Notes: Schedule semi-annual access review of Workspace roles in compliance calendar.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for enabling and enforcing the use of two-step verification on privileged administrator accounts.
Notes: Critical: enforce hardware-key 2SV on all Super Admin and Delegated Admin accounts; verify in Admin Console.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for establishing procedures to allocate the initial password to access the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System to end-users when {{IDP}} password authentication is used.
Notes: Covered by onboarding runbook; new-hire receives temp password via secure channel and 2SV is required on first login.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for configuring third party Marketplace apps permissions in the {{IDP}} Services consistent with their policies.
Notes: Set Marketplace to admin-approved-only; document allowlist review cadence.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for restricting access to and monitoring the use of Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) available in the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System.
Notes: Review OAuth scopes and API access in Admin Console; restrict to admin-approved apps.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for configuring domain settings related to integration with other systems within the customer's environment consistent with customer policies.
Notes: SAML/SSO and SPF/DKIM/DMARC documented in tenant baseline.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for ensuring that user data is exported and deleted from the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System before or within a reasonable amount of time after termination.
Notes: Add Takeout / Vault hold step to offboarding runbook with defined SLA.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for ensuring appropriate physical security controls over all devices that access the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System.
Notes: Covered by Asset Management / Device policy.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for ensuring any devices that access the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System or contain customer data are properly handled secured and transported as defined by the products requirements.
Notes: Covered by Device / Endpoint policy; MDM enrollment required.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for configuring the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System mobile device options consistent with customer policies and procedures.
Notes: Configure {{IDP}} MDM / Endpoint Verification per device policy.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for enabling logging and monitoring functionalities to detect administrator activity customer support activity security events system errors and data deletions to support customer incident management processes.
Notes: Export Admin / Login / Drive / OAuth audit logs to Cloud Logging or SIEM; align retention to Logging Policy.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for considering information security requirements in the deployment configuration and modification of their instance of the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System.
Notes: Tenant baseline documented; duplicate of CC1.5.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for establishing responsibilities and procedures to respond to relevant information security incidents pertaining to the use of the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System.
Notes: Covered by Incident Response Policy.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for ensuring that individuals creating and/or updating profiles or changing the product configurations are authorized.
Notes: Admin Console role-based access; covered by Access Control Policy.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for reviewing and testing features builds and product releases including Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to evaluate their impact prior to deploying into production environments as applicable.
Notes: Release Notes monitored; applies if customer deploys Apps Script in production.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for configuring test and/or development environments in their instance of the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System as applicable and restricting access to data in these environments.
Notes: No separate Workspace dev/test tenant.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for ensuring they have business recovery and backup procedures over their non-{{IDP}} managed information systems that access the {{IDP}} Application Programming Interfaces and Developer Offerings System.
Notes: Covered by BCP/DR Policy.

CUEC: Customers are responsible for developing and maintaining disaster recovery and business continuity plans for their non-{{IDP}} managed business systems.
Notes: Covered by BCP/DR Policy.

CUEC: Enabling SAML for their Enterprise Cloud accounts.
Notes: Confirm {{VCS}} Org SAML SSO is configured and bound to {{IDP}} IdP. Without SAML, MFA still flows through Workspace via OAuth but identity is not centrally managed.

CUEC: Enabling two-factor authentication and ensuring members and collaborators require two-factor authentication; this includes the implementation and management of personal access tokens.
ACME Mapping: AC-03 (MFA); Access Control Policy §7 (Service Accounts and API Keys)
Notes: Verify Org → Settings → Authentication Security → require 2FA. Inventory PATs in Access Control Matrix; prefer fine-grained PATs with expiry over classic PATs.

CUEC: Administering and configuring repositories, including permissions, enabling required reviews for pull requests, and enabling required status checks before merging.
Notes: Verify branch protection on main + release branches: required reviewers, required status checks, linear history. Map to CM-XX evidence.

CUEC: Securing configuration of {{VCS}} CI/pipelines (see your {{VCS}} provider's CI security-hardening guide).
ACME Mapping: Secure Development Practices; Access Control Policy §7
Notes: Pin pipeline action/step versions to commit SHAs (not tags); restrict the CI job token's permissions; prefer OIDC federation to {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} over long-lived CI secrets.

CUEC: Manage user provisioning and deprovisioning (org members, outside collaborators).
Notes: Supports CUEC #1 (SAML)/#2 (2FA). {{VCS}} is in the Access Control Matrix; departures must remove org membership and revoke PATs.

CUEC: Enable secret scanning and push protection across repositories.
Notes: Supports CUEC #3 (repo configuration). {{VCS}} Advanced Security or built-in scanning depending on plan.

CUEC: Enable Dependabot alerts and security updates org-wide.
Notes: Supports CUEC #3. Alerts triaged per Patch Management Policy.

CUEC: Review {{VCS}} audit log periodically; consider streaming to centralized log / SIEM.
Notes: Supports CUEC #3. Audit log streaming requires Enterprise tier.

CUEC: Manage repository visibility (private vs public) and forking restrictions.
Notes: Supports CUEC #3. Default private; restrict forks for repos with Restricted classification.

CUEC: Report security issues with {{VCS}} services to {{VCS}} Support / Security Advisory channels.
Notes: Document {{VCS}} security contact and status page in IR runbook.
